_README: Follow-up questions on entries that already have a ruling. A slug listed here comes BACK into the stack (flagged 'needs detail') with this exact question replacing the generic prompt, so the review tool asks the narrow thing instead of the broad one. Delete a slug once its answer is in the ruling. Written by Claude after trying to build from the ruling and hitting a specific wall. NOTE: a slug here only surfaces if it matches a MECHANIC slug the stack derives from the audit — a card-name slug is inert.

arsenal-triggers.built: BUILT in v2.33: the face-up path, the trigger, and one enabler. A card put face up carries _faceUp/_upTurn on the card itself; the arrow's payload is STAMPED onto it (_arsPow, _arsGA) so '+2{p} this turn' / 'go again this turn' survive until it is played later that same turn and expire if it is not. Call in the Big Guns is wired (subject read as 'an arrow'; its first effect resolves whether or not the put happens, per the 2026-07-28 ruling). Dry Powder Shot, Swift Shot and Ridge Rider Shot are none -> full.
arsenal-triggers.stuck: TWO ENABLERS LEFT, and they are harder than Call in the Big Guns because each is an activated ability with a cost rather than a plain action: Bull's Eye Bracers ('Action - Destroy Bull's Eye Bracers: if you have no cards in your arsenal, you may put an arrow card from your hand face up into your arsenal. It gains +1{p} until end of turn') and Death Dealer ('Once per Turn Action - {r}:' same condition, rider 'draw a card'). Both gate on 'no cards in your arsenal', which means ZERO cards — with a second slot from New Horizon they would need both empty, unlike Call in the Big Guns which needs only a free slot. Bull's Eye Bracers also has its OWN rider (+1{p} until end of turn on the arrow), which is a second stamp on top of the arrow's own trigger. TWO PAYOFFS remain deliberately unclaimed: Entangling Shot needs tapping a hero (not modelled anywhere), and Spire Sniping's 'look at the top 2, then put them back in any order' is a REORDER, which opt is not — opt permits bottoming, which would be strictly more powerful than printed.
arsenal-triggers.question: For Bull's Eye Bracers: its rider says the arrow 'gains +1{p} UNTIL END OF TURN' where the arrows say 'this turn'. Same duration, or is 'until end of turn' meant to survive something 'this turn' does not? And should the +1 stack with Dry Powder Shot's +2 when the same arrow is set with Bracers (printed reading says yes: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6)? Also worth a reading: is a reorder-only deck manipulation worth a seventh prompt variant for Spire Sniping alone, or should it wait until a second card needs it?

charge.built: Nothing. Listed here because Crow's Nest and the deck -> arsenal path belong to Azalea's reload identity rather than to the arsenal trigger itself.
charge.stuck: Crow's Nest: 'Whenever an arrow is put face up into your arsenal from your deck, you may pay {r}. If you do, put an aim counter on it.' The optional-cost machinery for this exists (v2.28) and the aim op exists; only the deck->arsenal move is missing.
charge.question: Is the deck -> arsenal path worth building for the solo trainer at all, given the dummy never uses it, or does it wait for a real Azalea pass? If it is built, does the arrow go face up immediately (visible to both players) — which is what 'face up' implies and what makes Crow's Nest's aim counter a real decision?

phantasm.built: Phantasm IS enforced — the trainer pops an attack blocked by a 6+ power card at declaration. What is missing is a HOOK: nothing fires when that destruction happens.
phantasm.stuck: Silent Stilettos reads 'Whenever an attacking ally you control dies OR an attack action card you control is destroyed by phantasm, you may pay {r}{r}{r}. If you do, destroy Silent Stilettos and gain 1 action point.' Three walls: two trigger conditions in one clause with no hook for either (no ally-death schedule; phantasm destruction is inline and fires nothing); a compound payload that destroys its own SOURCE, a shape nothing else in the pool has; and a 3-resource cost payable during the OPPONENT's turn, which the trainer can only satisfy from floated resources because there is no pitching mid-block.
phantasm.question: Given resources fizzle at end of turn and the trainer has no mid-block pitch, is this card effectively dead in solo play? If so it should be recorded as knowingly inert rather than built into a prompt that can never be afforded. If it should work, the prerequisite is pitching during defence, not the phantasm hook.
